text:
ana: Quick sync from onboarding lab 1 two users hit confusing behavior: py raised a generic RuntimeError for an expired token and one session showed a raw 429 with no body so the sample-app surfaced a traceback.

ryan: That's noisy. We need a compact, stable error contract that SDKs parse into typed exceptions. Otherwise UIs can't map to friendly copy.

chi: Agree. Proposal: server returns a tiny JSON body for errors with keys: `id`, `status`, `message`, optional `ttl_retry` (seconds), optional `user_action`. Example: `{ id: "auth.token_expired", status: 401, message: "API token expired", user_action: "reauth" }`.

marco: For rate limits include `ttl_retry` and `transient=true`. Example: `{ id: "rate.limit_exceeded", status: 429, message: "Rate limit exceeded", ttl_retry: 12, transient: true }`. SDKs should expose these on typed exceptions.

ana: (typo) meant ana: We should be careful about field names. `id` vs `code` vs `error_id`? I prefer `id` or `error_id` to make it obviously machine-stable.

ryan: Small API decision: prefer `error_id` for clarity. Keep `status` for http code to avoid `status_code`/`http_status` bikeshed. Keep `ttl_retry` to signal seconds.

chi: SDK behavior: parse JSON when present, raise typed subclasses that subclass existing exceptions (so old broad catch clauses still work). E.g., `RedwoodError` -> `RedwoodAuthError`, `RedwoodRateLimitError`, `RedwoodClientError`, `RedwoodServerError`. Each exposes attributes: `error_id`, `status`, `ttl_retry`, `transient`, `raw_body`.

marco: Sample python snippet for sample-apps (short): ```py
try:
  client.generate(...)
except RedwoodRateLimitError as e:
  sleep(e.ttl_retry or 1)
  retry()
except RedwoodAuthError:
  start_reauth()
except Exception as e:
  show_banner("Service temporarily unavailable. Try again.")
  if DEBUG: show_debug(e.raw_body or str(e))
```

ana: UI ask: default to friendly copy. Only show raw tracebacks if dev toggle enabled. Include canned support replies for common IDs (auth.token_expired, rate.limit_exceeded).

ryan: CI: add a tiny test in sample-apps that mocks 401 and 429 JSON bodies and asserts the app shows friendly copy and that SDK exceptions expose attributes. Gate SDK PRs on that.

chi: Backcompat: if server returns no JSON body, SDKs fall back to existing exception types and fill `status` from response headers. Also emit a debug log so we can track how often body missing.

marco: Naming nit: use `ttl_retry` (seconds) rather than `retry_after` to avoid timezone/format issues. `transient` boolean helps apps decide retry policy quickly.

ana: I'll draft a short RFC with the JSON shape, example payloads, and a tiny migration note showing how to switch from catch-all RuntimeError to typed exceptions. Will include paste-ready support text.

ci-bot: CI: sample-apps/error-handling-tests passed on branch error-id-contract (build #210) :white_check_mark:

ryan: Owners: ana (support copy + sample-app UI), chi (SDK parity + exceptions), marco (RFC + server example). ETA EOW. If anyone has hot takes on `error_id` vs `code` drop them now.

chi: +1 for `error_id`. Also adding convenience method `is_retryable()` on exceptions to centralize logic.

ana: (ana) +1. Small win for onboarding if we avoid showing raw tracebacks to end users.

marco: Thanks everyone 1 will open the RFC PR shortly.
